title: Take a link out for maintenance without losing purchases

blocks.text: An acquirer runs two links, `acq-mux` and a second one, behind a pool with `check-enabled`, and one sign-on manager per link. Every Tuesday night operations take `acq-mux` out for maintenance by stopping its manager, and every Wednesday morning there are complaints:

items: a handful of purchases routed to `acq-mux` during the maintenance stop came back declined;
the host's operators ask why they keep receiving an 0800 with code 002 on connections that never signed on, and on links that are down;
when the manager is deployed again, `acq-mux` sometimes stays out of the pool until the next day, and sometimes only when the host did not answer the 002.

blocks.text: The manager's per-link logic is `LinkSession` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/LinkSession.java`. `step()` works. Write `signOff()`, which the manager calls when it is stopped. About five lines.
The tests use a plain `TSpace`, write the adaptor's ready entry themselves, and play the host through the `Exchanger`.

cases.says: a signed-on link is signed off with 002 and is out of service afterwards
the link leaves service before 002 goes out, so no purchase is routed to it while it signs off
only the connection that signed on is signed off, told apart by identity even from an equal Date
a link with no connection gets no sign-off, whatever logon mark is left over
the session is forgotten at sign-off, so a manager deployed again signs the same connection on and the link returns
the session ends at sign-off whether or not the host answered the 002

origin.section: 11.5 Take a Link Out of Service Before You Sign It Off

concepts: At a planned stop the link leaves service before the 002, the 002 goes only to the connection that signed on, and the session is forgotten whatever the host answered.
